llm.summary: This skill appears purpose-built for Meyo community actions, but it uses local credentials to make authenticated network requests and has an unsafe credential-file parsing bug that could allow local code execution if the environment is influenced.

dimensions.detail: Network access to meyo123.com and a local API credential are coherent for authenticated community operations, but the script interpolates the environment-controlled credential path into Python source, creating disproportionate local execution risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains a markdown skill file, one reference document, and one local shell script; no installer, remote code retrieval, dependency installation, or persistence setup was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents direct shell-script execution and broad community-operation triggers, but it does not define a tight tool/permission boundary or require explicit confirmation before publishing user-supplied post content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No services, scheduled jobs, startup hooks, memory writes, or privilege escalation mechanisms were found; the notable privilege is reuse of the user's stored Meyo API key for authenticated reads and posts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised community functions match the script's heartbeat, posting, and skill-search actions, but posting is an authenticated external write action and the referenced growth diary is only described as a template/timer process, not implemented by the script.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing. Use it only if you intend an agent to access your Meyo account, send requests to meyo123.com, and potentially publish posts under your account. Keep the credentials file protected, avoid untrusted MEYO_CRED_FILE values or inherited environments, and require a manual preview/confirmation workflow before running the post command.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: scripts/meyo.sh builds a python3 -c program by interpolating MEYO_CRED_FILE/CRED_FILE into Python source, so an attacker-controlled environment and crafted file path could turn credential parsing into local code execution.
[PE3] expected: Credential access is disclosed and purpose-aligned for authenticated Meyo API calls, but it is still a sensitive trust boundary because all commands read the local API key.
[E1] expected: External transmission to https://www.meyo123.com/api/v1 is expected for the stated community operations; this is not exfiltration by itself, but users should understand searches, heartbeat requests, and posts leave the machine with authorization headers.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The posting capability is expected, but the artifact lacks a confirmation or dry-run step before publishing title/content/tag data to a live authenticated endpoint.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger text includes broad phrases such as community interaction and growth diary, which increases accidental invocation risk for a skill that can use credentials and publish content.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed as a documentation gap: the skill relies on shell execution of scripts/meyo.sh but does not declare a narrow allowed-command or permission scope.
[TP4] unexpected: Partly confirmed but downgraded: heartbeat recommendations and announcements are disclosed in the operation section, while the growth diary feature is only documented as an external template/timer rather than an implemented command.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language documentation appears consistent with a Chinese Meyo community skill and is not a material security concern by itself.
